profile.headline: Software Engineer at Cisco
profile.geoLocationName: Chapel Hill, North Carolina, United States
profile.summary: I am a Senior Software/Firmware Engineer at Secmation, where I work on designing new security architectures for embedded systems ranging from UAS to ICS. I am passionate about security and solving difficult design challenges. I am most engaged when learning or researching new technologies in order to overcome a challenge that is technical, logistical, and business in nature.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
As a critical member of the Hardware Firmware Security Team I am responsible for developing, supporting and integrating Cisco's hardware Root of Trust across Cisco’s different product lines (Catalyst 9K, ISR4K, ASR9k, etc). I work on a variety of challenging problems ranging from architectural design decisions, to managing development, testing, SCM, and releases for 20+ projects in various stages of development.

I work in a fast-paced environment. The HFST team has 50+ hardware designs under active development at any given time. I have succeeded in this environment because I am able to multitask, prioritize tasks, solve underlying issues, and bring a can-do problem-solving attitude. I have quickly become the subject matter expert for the Cisco Secure Boot Microloader, BIOS Protection, and UEFI, because of my self-starting attitude, strong investigative skills, ability to independently learn and solve problems, and strong communication ability. 

The technical aspect of my work involves adding Secure Boot support for new CPUs. I work with Assembly and Embedded C to perform chipset initialization and Cryptographic verification of the Bootloader (UEFI BIOS). I’ve used Python to automate and script Hardware and Software testing.

positions.title: Hardware Engineering Intern
positions.description: •	Accelerated the design process of RF filters by creating a MATLAB program that generated components in ANSYS HFSS, ran analysis on completed simulations and generated automated reports based on the results

positions.title: Team Leader - Firefighting Drone Challenge
positions.description:
Participated in a special topics course where we competed with other teams to develop a sensor module for a Firefighting drone. As part of this challenge I did the following:
•	Led an efficient and effective team that built a sensor module, which was used by every single team in the next semester of the challenge by creating a schedule to reach project goals and assigning roles and responsibilities to team members
•	Improved sensor module performance by designing tests, running tests, writing a MATLAB program that took testing data and created reports that helped interpret test results, which enabled the team to rapidly iterate the design of the system
•	Adapted an existing PRU Assembly program to meet specific needs of this project
•	Co-authored a design document detailing wiring and power distribution of entire drone
•	Heavily contributed to writing the end of semester report documenting the design, testing results and detailing wiring and power distribution of entire drone
